visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A middle-aged male presenter with short black hair and glasses, wearing a dark button-down shirt, stands centrally against a background featuring a large, stylized cat face. Bold white text overlay at the top reads '烏龜的 MBTI'. He speaks with high facial engagement and expressive open-palm gestures. (2) The visual transitions to a high-contrast screen capture of a scientific journal article titled 'Evidence of mood states in reptiles' from Animal Cognition 2025. The layout is clean and academic, with standard black text on a white background. (3) The presenter returns to the frame, maintaining his previous posture. He holds a small black remote or clicker in his right hand, making periodic pointing motions toward the viewer. Bright yellow subtitles appear consistently at the bottom of the frame over a dark background. (4) A detailed technical diagram of an experimental square enclosure is displayed. It shows a grid with specific coordinate points labeled 'P', 'N', 'NP', 'M', and 'NN', with a small graphic of a turtle positioned at the entrance. (5) The presenter is shown again in a medium shot, his facial expressions shifting from serious to slightly comedic as he explains the 'pessimistic' vs 'optimistic' behaviors. The lighting is flat and bright, characteristic of a professional studio setup. (6) A dual-pane diagram appears illustrating 'Novel Object Test' and 'Novel Environment Test', featuring technical drawings of boxes with measurements like '930' and '970'. (7) The video concludes with the presenter leaning slightly forward, gesturing with both hands towards the bottom of the screen where the final CTA subtitles appear.

(6) [Logo]: Animal Cognition (2025) 28:52. [Slogan]: ORIGINAL PAPER. (7) [Subtitle]: 想知道看似無感的爬行動物. (8) [Subtitle]: 是否跟我們一樣. (9) [Subtitle]: 會有持續整天的長期情緒. (10) [Subtitle]: 科學家找來 15隻紅腿象龜. The music remains consistent in the background, serving as a high-arousal bed under the narration, which maintains a technical yet enthusiastic tone. The mix is tightly compressed, ensuring vocal dominance over the rhythmic BGM. (4) Periodic digital 'click' sound effects punctuate the explanation of the experimental diagrams. The ambient noise floor is virtually non-existent, indicating a clean studio recording. The sequence concludes with a slightly rising vocal cadence and a sharp hard cut on the final CTA.
